Detailed Description

Ambisonic panner.

Pans a mono sound source into B format (W, X, Y, Z). This always outputs the four channels in this order.

See also:
Pan2, LinPan2, DecodeB, RotateB, TiltB, TumbleB, ZoomB

PanB::PanB ( UGen const &  input,

Base PanB Constuctor, use the AR() and KR() versions in user code.

Generic UGen argument documentation: Arguments which are UGen type can be continuously controlled and these may generally be multichannel (although there are some exceptions). Arguments which are constant/literal values (e.g., float or int) are clearly not continuously controllable and not multichannel (therefore will generallly be applied identically to each channel should the UGen being created is made multichannel via other arguments. Arguments which are Buffer type may require a Buffer for some specific purpose (e.g, TableOsc uses a buffer for its wavetable) but single channel Buffer objects are also used to specify an array of literal values (e.g., LLine)

Parameters:
inputThe mono input source. This should be a single value or a single channel (multichannel UGen instances will be mixed to mono).
azimuthThe angle in the horizontal plane in radians. 0 is front, +ve is clockwise viewed from above. This should be a single value or a single channel (multichannel UGen instances will be mixed to mono).
elevationThe angle in the vertical plane in radians. 0 is ear-level, is directly above the head and is directly below the head. This should be a single value or a single channel (multichannel UGen instances will be mixed to mono).
distanceArbitrary scale distance parameter. 1 could be considered the distance from the centre to the loudspeaker on playback. Values less than 1 are closer, larger than 1 further away. This should be a single value or a single channel (multichannel UGen instances will be mixed to mono).
